title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading the Mosel and eating with it

steps.title: Reading the label
steps.body: A Mosel label shows the producer, the village plus vineyard, like Bernkasteler Doctor, the grape, the Prädikat, like Spätlese, the vintage and sometimes trocken. VDP estates use their own classification: Gutswein, Ortswein, Erste Lage and Grosse Lage, with GG, Grosses Gewächs, for dry top wines. The AP number shows official testing.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Off-dry Mosel Kabinett suits spicy Asian food, like Thai and Sichuan, and smoked fish. Dry Riesling suits trout, pork and sauerkraut. Spätlese suits roast pork with apples. Sweet Auslese and BA suit fruit desserts, foie gras and blue cheese. Serve at 7 to 10 degrees.

steps.prompt: Which food suits an off-dry Mosel Kabinett?
steps.explanation: Sugar and acidity calm chilli heat.

steps.body: Mosel Riesling ages remarkably. A 20-year-old Spätlese often tastes less sweet and more complex than a young one.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Labels show village, vineyard and Prädikat
Kabinett suits spicy food; Auslese suits desserts
